subject: Commitment Playbook: acceptance signals, sentinel tests, and cutover tempo

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the low-latency routing and the dedicated pool discussion, and the execs want a clear path-to-commit before we propose moving to Procurement. I promised to send a short list of what matters for us so you can put together an acceptance-track we can sign off on.

Top-level asks from ops + compliance:
- Concrete pass/fail for throughput & p95 latency on our sample traffic (see sample CSV attached)
- Data handling confirmation: KV cache behaviour, retention, and optional customer-managed KMS for keys
- Failure-mode evidence: how Redwood falls back to lower-tier model and how quality is monitored
- Proof of integration with our SSO and IAM (assertions we can test during pilot)

Can you sketch the acceptance-tests you recommend (smoke + sentinel + go/no-go) and a realistic cutover tempo (timeline + blocked owners) so we can review with our security & procurement teams next Tuesday?

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLine Health

Lydia — thanks for the clear asks, that helps. I put together a short commitment playbook below (first pass) that maps to the categories you flagged. Ben (engineering lead) is cc'd to confirm feasibility and owners.

Proposed acceptance-track (three signal tiers):
1) Smoke (platform readiness, 3 working tests) — pass if all complete in 2 business days
   - API auth + SSO login end-to-end (test assertion: token exchange & role enforcement)
   - Basic throughput test (1,000 concurrent short requests, <100ms median latency)
   - Key routing verification (requests routed to customer-dedicated pool)

2) Sentinel (realistic traffic, quality & failover) — pass if measured against acceptance thresholds over a 48-hour window
   - Throughput: sustained 200 req/min with P95 latency < 350ms for standard prompts
   - Quality: sample prompt concordance >= 92% against your reference set (we'll share evaluation harness)
   - Fallback: simulated GPU pool outage — automatic fallback to compatible quantized variant within 15s and traffic drain within 2 min with alerting fired

3) Go/no-go (evidence + stakeholder signoff) — pass when Deliverables and paperwork complete
   - Audit artifacts: logs, KV cache retention doc, KMS integration test results
   - Legal/procurement: signed SOW and security addendum, DocuSign link in MAP
   - Ops runbook: cutover checklist, rollback procedure, and owner matrix

Suggested timeline (pilot -> commitment):
- Week 0: MAP acceptance criteria alignment (this week)
- Week 1: Smoke tests and SSO proof-of-instrumentation (2 business days)
- Week 2: Sentinel run (48 hours) + quality review
- Week 3: Evidence handoff, procurement review, DocuSign

Deliverables we'll produce: MAP doc with owner assignments, test harness (eval-runner) configured to your sample CSV, SOC2 evidence checklist, and a cutover runbook.

Next steps: if this aligns, I'll ask Ben to schedule the smoke window and confirm the security test owner from our side. Would you prefer these windows in PST mornings or APAC-friendly slots?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Looping Karthik for acceptance-test specifics and to confirm resource commitments. Quick notes from engineering after a feasibility pass:

- Feasibility: All three tiers are implementable within the proposed tempo. We can spin a dedicated trial pool and a quantized fallback model.
- Test harness: we'll publish a small runner that consumes brightline-probe-tests.csv and emits metrics to a shared trace (we'll provide a public Drive link once ready).
- Ownership:
   * Redwood test lead: Ben Carter (we own runner + fallback sim)
   * BrightLine test lead: Lydia Park (provide reference set + signoff on quality thresholds)

Acceptance-tests (practical examples you can run):
- Smoke: curl auth + sample POST -> expect 200 and valid 'session_id' header; attach verify-auth.sh (stub)
- Sentinel: k6 scenario (48h) that validates P95 and concordance; candidate pass if p95 < 350ms and concordance >= 92%
- Fallback sim: orchestration kill on the primary pool (we simulate with a controlled drain) and assert model variant switch and alerting within 120s

Security/compliance calls: we will provide an evidence bundle for KV cache retention and KMS key-wrap test results. For procurement: we'll prepare a one-page SOW addendum with SLAs for p95 and availability for this pilot.

I'll schedule a 30-min smoke-window booking for next Wednesday morning PST; please confirm that works for Lydia.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
